correction_to_brief: Brief says the 16-kosh number was 'verified zero times' - stale. R124 verified it on v298 (commit 69a03fc7); this round re-verifies on v299. Now verified twice, on two versions, same threshold.
follow_ups: Descriptor design, if pursued, must also close the raw-pointer doors (forbid vitti aliases of koshes, mala cells holding kosh addresses, pointer arithmetic into kosh buffers) or accept frequent raw-pointer breaks on every growth - a type-system change, not just a descriptor change.

Value semantics, if pursued, must be scoped to flat small scalar koshes (or paired with the descriptor design to fix the ceiling); for large koshes it replaces the alias cliff with a performance cliff (3.7-30 ms per 1M-element assignment) plus a leak cliff (8 MB per assignment, no free).

Windows lazy commit, if pursued, should be allocation-path-only (fast path 4-5 instructions; slow path VirtualAlloc amortized); it brings Windows to parity with Linux's existing laziness, it does not beat Linux.
Document: threads NEVER for the current design (R123 WS3 gap v); reuse NO for naive bump reset (compiler-proven dead-object reuse is possible in principle but not implemented).
not_run: implementation (test and analysis only, designs not built)
full suite (no tree changes; v299 suite numbers stand)

evidence: vitti a = k works on v299 (a[0]=99 -> k[0]=99 and a[0]=99, exit 0); vitti is untyped, so a[i] cannot always go through a descriptor (would break nirmmita buffers, whose first 8 bytes are data, not a buffer pointer)
mala cell holding a kosh address works on v299 (m[0]=k; p=m[0]; p[0]=99 -> k[0]=99, exit 0); stored address dangles on kosh growth under descriptors unless mala cells are tracked/forbidden

vitti + int arithmetic gives raw pointers into kosh buffers (kosh + int refuses E_KOSH_GANIT, but vitti + int does not); those dangle on movement, and under descriptors movement happens on every doubling (frequent), not just at MAXCAP (rare)
descriptor needs stable storage (arena/heap, one per kosh, shared by aliases; stack-allocated or copied descriptors break aliasing)
claim1_descriptor_eliminates_64mib.verdict: PARTLY - true for kosh-typed accesses; false for the language as a whole; without closing the raw-pointer doors it trades a rare break (at MAXCAP) for a frequent break (on every growth)

claim2_descriptor_cost_1_3_cycles.cold_dependent: 255 ns/step (bench2, full-period permutation seed, loads actually miss; ~250x the 1-3-cycle claim at 3 GHz)
claim2_descriptor_cost_1_3_cycles.guess_or_measurement: GUESS - no benchmark, no hardware, no methodology cited; review says 'roughly'
claim2_descriptor_cost_1_3_cycles.hot_dependent_extra: 2.240 ns/step (descriptor chain hot 5.429 ns/step minus direct chain hot 3.189 ns/step, volatile, contiguous); at 3 GHz ~6.7 cycles, at 1.50 GHz TSC ~3.4 cycles - more than 1-3 cycles at any plausible core frequency above ~1.5 GHz
claim2_descriptor_cost_1_3_cycles.l1_hit_vs_miss: L1 hit latency is 4-5 cycles; L1 miss is 14+ cycles (L2), ~40 cycles (L3), ~200+ cycles (DRAM). Neither 1-3 nor 4-5 is the miss cost.
claim2_descriptor_cost_1_3_cycles.method: AMD EPYC 9D25, 4 vCPU, TSC 1.50 GHz, clock_gettime, volatile to force loads (non-volatile run eliminated the direct loop, 0.000 ns/elem, and is not used; bench3 cold run at 5.3 ns/step is INVALID (even seed made its generator degenerate, did not scatter) and is not used
claim2_descriptor_cost_1_3_cycles.throughput_array_loop: direct 0.276 ns/elem (0.41 TSC cycles), descriptor per-access load 0.272 ns/elem (0.41 TSC cycles) - difference ~0 (pipelined, 2 loads/cycle, L1 hit)
claim2_descriptor_cost_1_3_cycles.verdict: DOES NOT SURVIVE as stated - throughput ~0, hot dependent latency ~2.2 ns, cold dependent ~255 ns

cost_1m_elements.c_memcpy_8mb: 3.659 ms (2.3 GB/s on this VM, fresh destination, page faults included)
cost_1m_elements.extrapolated_1000_assignments: 3.7 s (builtin) to 30 s (loop), plus 1000 x 8 MB = 8 GB allocated and leaked (no free); arena 1 GiB bound hit long before 1000 assignments if arena-allocated; region-allocated 1000 copies = 64 GB VSZ, same ceiling, crashes at 16th copy under 1 GiB limit - value semantics ALONE does not fix the WS3 ceiling
cost_1m_elements.sutram_loop_copy: 0.061 s for build 1M + copy 1M (2M pushes), ~30 ms per 1M-element copy via loop; prints correct last element 999999

claim3_value_semantics_eliminates_alias_.generality: Deep copy copies pointers, not pointed-to data, for koshes of strings/nested koshes/nirmmita buffers (shallow at depth 2+); a[0] and k[0] (nested koshes) would still be the same object unless copy is recursive (O(total size); cyclic structures (kosh containing itself) loop forever or need cycle detection)
claim3_value_semantics_eliminates_alias_.verdict: PARTLY - true for flat scalar koshes only; not for nested/pointer koshes; not acceptable for large koshes (performance cliff + leak cliff, violates assignment-is-cheap intuition)

claim4_windows_lazy_commit_4_5_instructi.access_path: ZERO extra instructions (allocator ensures committed region covers all allocated memory before returning the pointer, so accesses never fault)
claim4_windows_lazy_commit_4_5_instructi.allocation_path: fast path ~4-5 instructions total (bump + cmp + jbe (2 instructions for the check) + return); check ONLY on allocation path
claim4_windows_lazy_commit_4_5_instructi.hello_world: drops from 1 GB to a few kilobytes (true for hello, 0 allocations); on Linux already true without change (R124 WS2: 16 KB RSS / 0.2 MB VSZ via MAP_NORESERVE) - Windows lazy commit brings Windows to parity with Linux, does not beat Linux
claim4_windows_lazy_commit_4_5_instructi.kosh_regions: each region needs its own committed_cursor (or commit on growth in chunks, not at creation: new kosh capacity 4 commits only 4 KB, one page, not 64 MB, growing on demand)
claim4_windows_lazy_commit_4_5_instructi.slow_path: once per 1 MiB chunk, VirtualAlloc (MEM_COMMIT) syscall - hundreds of cycles + kernel transition, NOT 4-5 instructions, but amortized over 1 MiB (131072 x 8-byte allocations -> ~0.008 cycles per allocation, negligible)

reviewer_closed_answers.reuse_in_live_block: NO - concurred as a design decision (bump allocator cannot know an object is dead; naive reset corrupts live aliases); compiler-proven dead-object reuse is possible in principle but not implemented, not trivial
reviewer_closed_answers.threads: NEVER - concurred for the current design (single global arena cursor races; thread-local arenas and per-kosh locks/atomics are a redesign, not a fix; out of scope for v1.0; reference should say so (R123 WS3 gap v))

ws2.mala_alias: m1 = mala_nava(4) (yoj mala); m2 = m1; m2[0] = 99; m1[0] prints 99, exit 0 - mala assignment via vitti copies the buffer address, not the elements; reviewer proposed value semantics for kosh only, not mala, so mala still aliases
ws2.nirmmita_alias: p = nirmmita(16); q = p; q[0] = 99; p[0] prints 99, exit 0 - vitti assignment copies the address, not the buffer; nirmmita MUST alias (buffers, FFI, slice idiom: string + int pointer arithmetic is aliasing by design)
ws2.verdict: TRUE that value semantics for kosh closes one door and leaves two open; FALSE that aliasing simply does not exist for the language; escape analysis does NOT become trivial overall (only for kosh; nirmmita/mala escapes still need analysis, e.g. E_SCRATCH_ESCAPE)

ws3.1000_kosh_ulimit: segfault exit 139 (before printing made 1000, consistent with crashing at the 16th)
ws3.16_kosh_ulimit: made 1..15, then segfault exit 139 during 16th creation
ws3.new_design_few_kilobytes_for_1000: LOOSE - value semantics alone: 1000 copies = 1000 regions = 64 GB VSZ, crashes at 16th copy; descriptor design with bump buffers: 1000 x 24 bytes + 1000 x 8 bytes = 32 KB (a few TENS of kilobytes, not a few kilobytes); per-buffer mmap pages: 1000 x 4 KB = 4 MB; spirit (orders of magnitude smaller than 64 GB) true, letter (a few KB) true only for hello (0 collections)
ws3.reviewer_1000_would_crash: TRUE, but threshold is 16, not 1000 (any N >= 16 crashes; 1000 is just an example of many)
ws3.verdict: VERIFIED (twice: v298 in R124, v299 here, same threshold)
